title: Does your prayer tell us how to spend our money?
subtitle: Mocking the idea that prayer reaches business
then: Shu'ayb had told Madyan to stop cheating in weights and measures. They mocked him: does {trap}your prayer{/trap} order us to leave our fathers' gods, or to stop doing what we like with our wealth? Ibn Abbas and others said that calling him {trap}the forbearing, the right-minded{/trap} was sarcasm.
now: You pray on time, then fudge the timesheet or overcharge a customer who will never notice. A colleague says, "Religion has nothing to do with business." {idea}Shu'ayb's people said the same.{/idea} Real prayer walks with you into the shop and the spreadsheet.
old: My prayer is between me and Allah; how I handle money is a separate matter.
new: Prayer is meant to shape how I earn and spend, not stay on the prayer mat.
try: Check one transaction or bill you handle today and make sure it is fully fair.

title: I only want to fix things, as much as I can.
subtitle: Shu'ayb practices what he asks of others

row.title: no double standard
sub: I do not do what I forbid

row.title: reform
sub: as far as I am able

then: Shu'ayb answered calmly. He had clear guidance and good provision from his Lord. Qatadah explained his words: {idea}I do not forbid you something while doing it myself.{/idea} He only wanted reform as far as he could, and said {reward}my success is only through Allah{/reward}.
now: You tell your kids to put the phone away at dinner while yours is in your hand. You ask your team to be on time and you walk in late. {idea}Advice lands when your life matches it.{/idea} Then leave the result to Allah.
old: I can tell others what is right even if I do not do it myself.
new: I give advice best by living it, and I rely on Allah for the result.
try: Pick one thing you often tell others to do, and do it yourself today first.

title: Do not let your dislike of me ruin you.
subtitle: Spite against the messenger as a trap

row.title: the grudge
sub: I will not let him be right

then: Shu'ayb warned his people: {trap}do not let your hatred of me push you to persist{/trap} in corruption. Otherwise you may meet what struck the peoples of Nuh, Hud and Salih. And Lut's people were not far off. Qatadah said they had only been destroyed yesterday, as it were.
now: Your sister gives you good advice about your marriage, but because it is her, you do the opposite. Your coworker is right about the plan, but you dislike him. {trap}Spite can make you reject what helps you.{/trap}
old: I cannot take advice from someone I do not like.
new: My dislike of a person should never push me away from a truth they carry.
try: Think of advice you dismissed because of who said it. Take one honest look at it today.

title: My Lord is Merciful and Loving.
subtitle: After the warning, the door to return

row.title: Al-Wadud
sub: who loves the one who returns

then: Right after warning of past nations, Shu'ayb opened the door. {idea}Ask your Lord's forgiveness for past sins and repent for what is ahead.{/idea} Then he described Allah: {reward}Merciful and Loving{/reward} toward those who repent.
now: You slipped back into the same habit again last night and feel too ashamed to pray. You think He must be tired of you. {reward}He is Loving to the one who returns.{/reward} The warning was never meant to shut the door.
old: After so many relapses, Allah must be done with me.
new: Allah is Merciful and Loving, and returning to Him is always welcome.
try: Make wudu and pray two rakat tonight, asking forgiveness for one specific thing.

title: If not for your clan, we would have stoned you.
subtitle: Truth dismissed because its speaker seems weak

row.title: your clan
sub: the only reason we hold back

then: Ath-Thawri said Shu'ayb was called {idea}the orator of the prophets{/idea}, yet his people said they did not understand much of what he said. They saw him as weak, only one man. {trap}Only respect for his clan stopped them from stoning him.{/trap}
now: In the family WhatsApp group, the quiet cousin with no degree says something wise and nobody replies. The same idea from the rich uncle gets ten hearts. {idea}Truth does not depend on who backs the speaker.{/idea}
old: I listen to people based on how important they are.
new: A true word deserves attention whoever says it and whoever stands behind them.
try: Reply warmly today to someone whose comment usually gets ignored.

title: You fear my clan more than you fear Allah?
subtitle: Throwing Allah behind your back
then: Shu'ayb asked: {trap}is my clan more weighty to you than Allah?{/trap} You would leave me alone out of regard for my tribe, but not out of awe of the Lord. They had {trap}thrown Him behind their backs{/trap}. But {idea}my Lord surrounds all that you do{/idea}.
now: You would never shout at your mother in front of guests, but alone you do. You drive the speed limit only near the camera. {idea}You are never alone with Him.{/idea} The question is whose gaze really holds you back.
old: What really stops me is what people will think.
new: Allah sees everything I do, and His awareness should matter more than anyone's.
try: Notice one thing you do only when no one is watching, and do it as if He is watching, because He is.

title: Do your work, I am doing mine. Wait and see.
subtitle: Parting words when the arguing is over
then: When Shu'ayb gave up hope of their response, he said: {trap}act according to your way, and I will act according to mine{/trap}. Ibn Kathir calls this a severe threat. Soon they would know who would be disgraced and who was lying. {idea}Wait, and I will wait with you.{/idea}
now: The argument in the comment thread has gone 40 replies. The family debate about honesty in business keeps circling. {idea}At some point you stop arguing and just keep doing right.{/idea} Your conduct will speak when words do not.
old: I need to keep arguing until the other side admits I am right.
new: After I have spoken clearly, I can stop arguing and let my conduct and time speak.
try: Leave one ongoing argument today with a calm last line and get on with doing good.

title: A single cry, and they lay still in their homes.
subtitle: Shu'ayb saved, the wrongdoers seized
then: Allah saved Shu'ayb and the believers {reward}by mercy from Him{/reward}. The wrongdoers were seized by {trap}a mighty cry{/trap} and lay lifeless in their homes. Ibn Kathir notes other surahs mention a quake and a shadow cloud; here the cry is mentioned because of how disrespectfully they spoke to their prophet.
now: Think of how you talk to the people Allah sent into your life to guide you: parents, teachers, the imam. {idea}How you speak matters to Allah.{/idea} Respect in words is part of faith.
old: Harsh words are just words; they do not count for much.
new: The way I speak to those who guide me is weighed by Allah.
try: Speak to a parent or teacher today with deliberate gentleness, even if you disagree.

title: As if they had never lived there at all.
subtitle: Madyan gone, like its neighbor Thamud

row.title: a passing stay
sub: gone as if it never was

then: After the cry, Madyan's homes stood {trap}as if no one had ever prospered in them{/trap}. They went away just as Thamud had. Ibn Kathir says Thamud were their neighbors, {idea}similar in disbelief and in highway robbery{/idea}.
now: You drive past the shop that was always busy and now has a for-lease sign. The house you grew up in has strangers in it. {idea}Every place we fill is a passing stay.{/idea} What will you have sent ahead when you leave yours?
old: My home, business, and wealth feel permanent.
new: Everything I have built here is temporary; only what I send ahead remains.
try: Give something today from what you have, money, food, or time, as something sent ahead.

title: Musa came with signs and clear authority.
subtitle: The last story in the surah's series

row.title: clear authority
sub: an argument they could not answer

row.title: enough proof
sub: if only we had seen more

then: After Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb, the surah briefly tells of Musa. Allah sent him {idea}with His signs and clear proofs{/idea} to Fir'awn, king of the Copts, and his chiefs. {trap}The proof was not lacking.{/trap}
now: You tell yourself you would pray more if you only felt a sign, a dream, a clear moment. Yet the signs are already there: the breath you took, the morning you woke to. {idea}The proof is not missing. Attention is.{/idea}
old: If I saw a clear sign, I would finally change.
new: Allah has already sent clear signs; what I need is the will to respond.
try: Write down three signs of Allah you saw today without looking for anything special.

title: They followed Fir'awn, and he was no guide.
subtitle: Following the powerful over the proof
then: Musa came to Fir'awn and his chiefs, {trap}but they followed Fir'awn's command{/trap}, his path and methods of transgression. Ibn Kathir says there was {trap}no right guidance in it{/trap}, only ignorance, misguidance and stubbornness.
now: Your team lead tells you to hide a defect from the client, and everyone goes along because he signs the reviews. {idea}Rank is not the same as right.{/idea} You can be respectful and still refuse to follow wrong.
old: If the person in charge says so, it is not my responsibility.
new: Power does not make a command right, and I answer for whom I follow.
try: If you are asked to do something unfair today, politely ask once: is there an honest way to do this?

title: The leader walks ahead, and they follow him in.
subtitle: Followers end where their leader ends

row.title: just this life
sub: it is only work, only habit

then: Ibn Kathir says that {trap}just as they followed Fir'awn in this life, he will lead them on the Day of Resurrection{/trap}. He will walk ahead of his people into the Fire. Those who lead others into wrong carry a heavy share. {idea}Following is never neutral.{/idea}
now: Your feed is shaped by the voices you follow. Your habits are shaped by the friends you copy. {idea}Every follow is a direction.{/idea} Choose leaders you would be glad to walk behind on the Day.
old: Who I follow online or in life is a small, harmless choice.
new: The ones I follow are walking me somewhere, in this life and the next.
try: Unfollow one account that pulls you away from Allah, and follow one that pulls you closer.

title: A curse here and on the Day, a wretched gift.
subtitle: What followers of Fir'awn received
then: Fir'awn's followers were {trap}pursued by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection{/trap}. Mujahid said another curse is added on that Day, so there are two. Ibn Abbas called it {trap}the curse of this life and the next{/trap}, the evil gift they were given.
now: You stayed quiet about the wrong at work to keep your bonus. You laughed along to keep your place in the group. {idea}Ask what that loyalty is really paying you.{/idea} The reward of following wrong is never what it promises.
old: Going along with the powerful pays off.
new: Whatever following wrong seems to give, its real gift is loss, here and after.
try: Think of one place where you go along with wrong to keep a benefit. Take one small step out.
